title: Derived coherent duality for proper flat algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a proper, flat, finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Flatness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts; proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. Use the derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ of module sheaves on the small etale site, and its full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $Rf_*$ for pushforward computed by K-injective resolutions and $Lp^*$ for tensor pullback computed by K-flat resolutions. There exists a relative dualizing pair $(K_f,\tau_f)$, with $K_f\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\tau_f:Rf_*K_f\to\mathcal O_T$. The complex $K_f$ is locally bounded and pseudo-coherent (on etale affine charts it is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free modules). For every affine $a:V=\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$, put $X_V=X\times_TV$, $p:X_V\to X$ and $f_V:X_V\to V$. Composition with the pulled-back trace induces, for every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X_V})$, a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{X_V})}(E,Lp^*K_f)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(R\Gamma(X_V,E),A[0]).$$
The pair is unique up to a unique trace-preserving isomorphism. For every scheme morphism $a:T'\to T$, $Lp^*K_f\simeq K_{f_{T'}}$ as trace pairs; these isomorphisms respect identity and iterated base change. When $X,T$ are schemes with $T$ affine, this pair agrees, under the Zariski-etale derived quasi-coherent comparison, with $f^!\mathcal O_T$ and its adjunction trace, where $f^!$ denotes the right adjoint of $Rf_*$ on derived quasi-coherent modules. No dimension, smoothness, Gorenstein or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0E5X (definition-relative-dualizing-proper-flat) and following Hom characterization; 0E5Z (lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing); 0E61 (lemma-existence-relative-dualizing); 0E6C (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing); 0E6E (lemma-compare). Relative perfectness and hence local boundedness: spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0DKN (definition-relatively-perfect).

proof.text: Over an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ mapping to $T$, the space $X_V$ is qcqs (it is proper over the affine $V$). Choose the right adjoint $a_V$ and its counit from [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-pushforward-right-adjoint], and set $W_V=a_V(\mathcal O_V)$ with $t_V=\epsilon_{f_V,\mathcal O_V}$. Adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(E,W_V)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{V,*}E,\mathcal O_V)$ by $u\mapsto t_V\circ Rf_{V,*}u$. To obtain the stated $D(A)$ formula, use the equivalence $a_A:D(A)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_V)$ of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization]: its quasi-inverse is $R\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{et}},-)$, it sends $A[0]$ to $\mathcal O_V$ (the associated sheaf of $A$ has value $B\otimes_AA=B$ on $\operatorname{Spec}B$), and $R\Gamma(V,Rf_{V,*}E)=R\Gamma(X_V,E)$. The properties in [lem-sfb-affine-adjoint-unit-properties] give relative perfection, $Rf_{V,*}W_V\in D^{\le0}$ and $R\mathcal Hom(W_V,W_V)\simeq\mathcal O_{X_V}$. In particular $\operatorname{Hom}(W_V,W_V[i])=H^i(X_V,\mathcal O_{X_V})=0$ for $i<0$.

For any map $w:V^{\prime}\to V$ of affine schemes over $T$, [lem-sfb-affine-flat-proper-adjoint-base-change] supplies $Lw_X^*W_V\simeq W_{V^{\prime}}$ carrying the pulled-back counit trace to $t_{V^{\prime}}$; the pulled trace uses $\beta^{-1}$ from [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-pushforward-base-change]. This trace-compatible isomorphism is unique: both objects represent $E\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{V^{\prime},*}E,\mathcal O_{V^{\prime}})$, and compatibility with the counit makes the induced natural transformation the identity. Yoneda therefore identifies any two such maps and proves the identity and cocycle laws for successive affine maps.

source.place: 0E5I, 0E5L; discussion after 0E5X, uniqueness of the representing pair

proof.text: Choose $V_\bullet\to T$ using [lem-sfb-affine-etale-hypercover-refinement] and put $U_\bullet=X\times_TV_\bullet$. On each summand $X\times_TV_{n,i}$ take the affine-base object from step 1; disjoint union gives $W_n$ on $U_n$. Step 2 gives compatible simplicial identifications. Each negative self-Ext of $W_n$ is the product of the corresponding zero groups on its summands. Part (1) of [lem-sfb-space-negative-ext-hyperdescent] thus gives $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ restricting compatibly to every $W_n$. Relative perfection descends etale locally by [lem-sfb-space-relative-perfect-base-change]. Taking the module $f^{-1}\mathcal O_T$ itself in its finite Tor-amplitude condition shows $K$ is locally cohomologically bounded; its pseudo-coherence gives the claimed local finite-free bounded-above models.

source.place: 0E61, first paragraph through descent of the complex; 0DLA

proof.text: Put $C=Rf_*K$. By [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-pushforward-base-change], its restriction to each $V_{n,i}$ is $Rf_{n,i,*}W_{n,i}$, hence is in $D^{\le0}$ by [lem-sfb-affine-adjoint-unit-properties]. Thus $C\in D^{\le0}$; quasi-coherent cohomology is supplied by the same base-change node. For $i<0$, the group $\operatorname{Hom}(C|_{V_n},\mathcal O_{V_n}[i])$ vanishes: its source has cohomology in degrees $\le0$ and its target in degrees $\ge-i>0$, so [lem-pc-derived-tstructure-orthogonality] applies with bounds $0<-i$. The local traces $t_{n,i}$ agree on $V_1$ by step 2. Part (2) of [lem-sfb-space-negative-ext-hyperdescent], applied on $T$ to $(C,\mathcal O_T)$, gives a unique $\tau:C\to\mathcal O_T$ with these restrictions. This supplies the negative-Ext hypothesis omitted at the end of the source proof.

source.place: 0E61, last paragraph (omitted details for trace descent), using 0DL9

proof.text: Fix any affine $a:V\to T$ and write $p:X_V\to X$. By [lem-sfb-affine-etale-hypercover-refinement] choose an affine-component etale hypercover $V^{\prime}_\bullet\to V$ with a simplicial refinement $V^{\prime}_\bullet\to V_\bullet\times_TV$, so each $V^{\prime}_{n,j}$ maps over $T$ to some $V_{n,i}$. On $X\times_TV^{\prime}_{n,j}$, step 2 for the affine maps $V^{\prime}_{n,j}\to V_{n,i}$ and $V^{\prime}_{n,j}\to V$, with the composition law of [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-pushforward-base-change], identifies both $(Lp^*K,La^*\tau\circ\beta_K^{-1})$ and $(W_V,t_V)$ with $(W_{V^{\prime}_{n,j}},t_{V^{\prime}_{n,j}})$. Hence negative Exts between $Lp^*K$ and $W_V$, in either order, vanish on every term $X\times_TV^{\prime}_n$, being products of the negative self-Exts killed by [lem-sfb-affine-adjoint-unit-properties]. The local trace-compatible isomorphisms on $X\times_TV^{\prime}_0$ have equal pullbacks to $X\times_TV^{\prime}_1$ by the uniqueness in step 2, so part (2) of [lem-sfb-space-negative-ext-hyperdescent] on $X_V$ glues them to $\phi:Lp^*K\to W_V$ and their inverses to $\psi$; injectivity in part (2) gives $\psi\phi=1$, $\phi\psi=1$. Trace preservation follows from injectivity in part (2) on $V$ for $(Rf_{V,*}Lp^*K,\mathcal O_V)$: on each $V^{\prime}_n$ the source is $Rf_*W_{V^{\prime}_n}\in D^{\le0}$, so negative Homs to $\mathcal O$ vanish by [lem-pc-derived-tstructure-orthogonality] as in step 4. By step 1, $(K,\tau)$ has the universal Hom property for every affine $V\to T$. For two such pairs, the local representing isomorphisms over the $V_{n,i}$ are unique by Yoneda, satisfy the cocycle law, and glue on $X$ by the same negative cross-Ext argument, with traces compared by injectivity on $T$. This proves global existence and uniqueness of the trace pair.

source.place: 0E61 and 0E5Z; proof of 0E60 (lemma-covering-enough), affine refinements and morphism descent

proof.text: For arbitrary $a:T^{\prime}\to T$, define the pulled trace by $Rf^{\prime}_*Lp^*K\xrightarrow{\beta_K^{-1}}La^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{La^*\tau}\mathcal O_{T^{\prime}}$, with [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-pushforward-base-change]. Relative perfection of $Lp^*K$ follows from [lem-sfb-space-relative-perfect-base-change]. For an affine $V\to T^{\prime}$, its further pullback and trace are those for the composite $V\to T$ because the base-change comparisons in [lem-sfb-flat-space-derived-pushforward-base-change] compose. Step 5 therefore shows it is a dualizing pair for $f^{\prime}$. Uniqueness gives its trace-preserving isomorphism to $K_{f^{\prime}}$. Both comparisons for iterated base change preserve trace and are consequently equal by uniqueness; the identity comparison is proved the same way.

Finally assume $X,T$ are schemes and $T$ affine. The equivalences in [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison] identify Zariski and small-etale $Rf_*$ and their structure sheaves. Transport the adjunction of step 1 across these equivalences. It is a right adjunction for Zariski $Rf_*$, and its counit is the transported trace. Any chosen right adjoint $f^!$ is uniquely isomorphic to it, preserving the counit, by the representing Hom bijections. Evaluation at $\mathcal O_T$ gives precisely the comparison of pairs asserted in the item.
